defaults.permitted_development: Across Greater London, demolition is controlled by the GPDO and heritage legislation rather than treated as a free-standing general right. The route depends on what is being removed, whether Part 11 applies and whether the building or site is protected.

rules.height_rules: There is no demolition height allowance. Height matters because it affects method, sequencing, temporary works, visibility and the risk posed to adjoining land and buildings.
rules.depth_rules: There is no separate depth rule. Partial demolition and demolition tied to rebuilding have to be judged by the real scope of the works and by what remains on site afterwards.
rules.boundary_rules: Across Greater London, the practical boundary issues are usually neighbour safety, party structures, plant access, hoarding, highway occupation and the stability of anything left standing next door.
rules.roof_rules: Roof removal is not automatically a clean separate step. Once it forms part of wider demolition, heritage, structural stability and weatherproofing can alter the planning route.
rules.materials_rules: Salvage, asbestos, dust, waste removal and making good exposed faces are usually the live practical issues. Separate health, safety and building-control duties remain in play even where the planning route is clear.
